discovery: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson through the conception and construction of the ATLAS and CMS detectors at the LHC
motivation: The 2013 prize honoured the prediction of the Higgs mechanism; the experimental discovery, which made the Standard Model's scalar sector a measured fact, has not yet been recognised. Peter Jenni (founding spokesperson of ATLAS) and Michel Della Negra and Tejinder Virdee (founders of CMS) conceived these general-purpose detectors in the late 1980s and led their design and construction over two decades. Their concepts included the ATLAS air-core toroid and muon system, the CMS high-field solenoid, and precise crystal electromagnetic calorimetry. These choices made possible the independent 5-sigma observations of a 125 GeV boson in July 2012 in the diphoton and four-lepton channels. The same detectors now measure the Higgs couplings with precision and set the strongest collider limits on supersymmetry, dark matter and extended Higgs sectors. Their work provided an unambiguous, cross-checked discovery that fundamentally completed our picture of particle masses.
